hypotheses.justification: `differentialCoeff ω` is defined (Def_ModularCurve_CanonicalDivisor.lean) as `if h : ∃ f, ω = f • v.dCoord then h.choose else 0`, so it makes sense without any instance. Split on `subsingleton_or_nontrivial Ω[F⁄K]`. In the nontrivial case the existing proof applies unchanged. In the subsingleton case `D g = 0 = D 0`, so `v.differentialCoeff (D g) = v.differentialCoeff (D 0)`. By `hint 0 (zero_mem _)` this lies in `v.toValuationSubring`, so `R.res_of_mem` gives `R.res (...) = 0`. The conclusion therefore holds with or without the instance. It can be removed independently of `[v.DCoordGenerates]`.

Run the same induction on N. The base case uses only `hint` and `R.res_of_mem`. In the successor step, write g = g₁ + a·π^{-(N+1)} with g₁ ∈ poleSubmodule N, as the existing proof does via hsurj and `laurentTail_remainder_mem_poleSubmodule`; neither needs the instance. Leibniz plus `D_pow_succ_inv`, which is instance-free, give D(a·π^{-(N+1)}) = e • dCoord with e = algebraMap K F (c·(-(N+1)))·(π^(N+2))⁻¹. If dCoord = 0, then D g = D g₁ and the induction hypothesis finishes. If dCoord ≠ 0 and D g is not of the form f • dCoord, then differentialCoeff (D g) = 0 by `dif_neg`, and its residue is 0 by `map_zero`. If dCoord ≠ 0 and D g = f • dCoord, the coefficient is unique: from (x - f) • dCoord = 0 and `smul_eq_zero` over the field F, x = f. So differentialCoeff (D g) = f, and since D g₁ = (f - e) • dCoord, differentialCoeff (D g₁) = f - e. Hence res f = res (f - e) + res e = 0 + 0, by the induction hypothesis and `R.res_algebraMap_mul_uniformizer_pow_inv` (hn : 1 ≤ N+1). So the statement holds without the instance; it is used only by the lemmas called in the current proof. It can be removed independently of `[Nontrivial Ω[F⁄K]]`.
